neighbours.label: ' of' in 'center of mass' / 'centre of gravity' in a classical-mechanics passage (the slot where ' mass' comes next); not 'of mass' in general
fire: When no external force acts, the center of mass of the system moves in a straight line.
The torque about the pivot depends on where the centre of gravity of the beam lies.
Newton's second law tells us that the acceleration of the center of mass equals the net force divided by the total mass.
A thrown wrench spins, but its centre of mass follows a smooth parabola.
The Earth and Moon both revolve around their common centre of mass.
To balance the ladder, the support must sit under its center of gravity.
In a collision between two carts, the velocity of the center of mass stays unchanged.
For a rigid body, the motion of the centre of mass is governed by the sum of the external forces.
quiet: When no visitors come, the center of town is quiet and the shops close early.
The answer to the puzzle depends on where the centre of the maze lies.
The chemistry teacher explained that the conservation of mass holds in every reaction.
A thrown party is fun, but its centre of attention was the birthday cake.
The kilogram and the gram are both units of mass in the metric system.
To hang the picture, the nail must sit at the centre of the wall.
In a debate between two parties, the views of the centre of the electorate matter most.
For a growing city, the location of the centre of commerce is shaped by its roads.

notes: Card: peaks on ' of' before mass, plus inertia/Newton's-law tokens; the + pole promotes ' vertex'/' focus' (geometry centre) and suppresses ' mass'. Probes: 'centre of mass' 0.47-1.10, 'center of gravity' 0.64, but 'conservation of mass' 0.02, 'unit of mass' 0.04, 'centre of town' 0.14. Inertial-frame sentences also fire (0.28-0.46), so the label is narrower than the pole.
